text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, choose clear, meaningful endpoints that describe resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened: 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation is essential because it helps other developers understand how to use your API without guessing. Finally, use versioning, for example /api/v1/, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. Following these simple practices saves time and reduces confusion for everyone.
